slides.heading: Integers
slides.body: Integers is part of Variables and Primitive Data Types. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: Integers
slides.body: An integer is a whole number without a decimal point. It is useful for counts, scores, ages, and other exact whole-number values.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: An integer is like counting chairs in a room. You count 1, 2, 3, not 1.5 chairs.

slides.heading: Key Rule
slides.body: Use clear variable names and match the data type to the kind of value you need to store.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Store your age in a variable named age and print it.
slides.hint: Use a whole number, then print(age).
